title: CLO Account Integration User Guide
content: *This FAQ is intended for existing CLO users. # **Objective** **Access all CLO Virtual Fashion services using a single email account.** This FAQ will cover the updates and changes to login methods for **CLO** **Individual** & **Student** license account types. This change will not affect Enterprise & Academic account types at this time. Please check the [general FAQ](https://clovf.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/sections/9021928318863-General) if you have questions about the account merging process (CLO-SET accounts). # **Details** **1) Change in login method** **Effective from the next released version, CLO 2024.0** **What does this cover?** CLO website / Software version 2024.0 and above | **Software Version** **(7.3 and below)** | **Software Version** **Above 2024.0** ---|---|--- **How to login** | **Existing License ID & Password** | **CLO-SET ID & Password ** **2) How do I get a “CLO-SET ID & Password” if I have an existing CLO account? ** Check out our detailed step-by-step guide **[here](https://clovf.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/9021921372047-Account-Merging-from-CLO-SET)**. **3) What is the difference between a CLO-SET account and my previous CLO account?** With your old CLO account you had to have multiple logins to access all of the CLO Virtual Fashion (CVF) products and services. Now with one CLO-SET account you can access all CLO Virtual Fashion services without additional logins. If you choose to login to the websites for any of the CLO Virtual Fashion (CVF) products and services you will be prompted to merge your account logins into a CLO-SET account. **4) How do I login to CLO / Marvelous Designer / Jinny after I merge my account?** You can login to CLO / Marvelous Designer / Jinny with your CLO-SET ID & Password. **5) I have a subscription license for CLO and I like to use an older version than 2024.0. Do I have to use a different Log in or can I use the CLO-SET account?** * If you have an old installer on your device and you have access to versions below 2024.0: Use the older login method. Login to the installed version you wish to use with your License ID & Password (same as before) * For 2024.0 and above: you can log in to all CLO Virtual Fashion product (CLO/Marvelous Designer/CONNECT/CLO-SET) websites and software with your CLO-SET account. **6) I have both CLO and Marvelous Designer accounts and I use them frequently. How does it affect me?** You no longer have to use two separate logins! You can continue using your licenses without functional change for both CLO and Marvelous Designer. All you have to do is login with your CLO-SET account. You can check the license information for your products on the CLO or Marvelous Designer websites. **7) I like to use different email addresses for CLO and Marvelous Designer for my own reasons and want to keep them separate. Can I still have separate accounts?** Yes, make sure to use the different email addresses for your CLO-SET merge so that you will have two separate CLO-SET accounts. The accounts are tied to each email address and the licenses associated with each account will be included in that merge. If you wish to unify your email addresses in the future or have other questions, please contact us by [submitting a request](https://clovf.zendesk.com/hc/requests/new). **If you need assistance regarding accounts merging or have questions, please contact us by[submitting a request](https://clovf.zendesk.com/hc/requests/new)****, and our support team will promptly respond to your inquiry.**** **
content_description: This FAQ page provides existing CLO users with essential information on the updated login methods for accessing all CLO Virtual Fashion services through a single CLO-SET account.

title: Can I change my ID or email address?
content: **Question** Can I change my ID or email address? **Answer** With the integrated CLO-SET account, auto-generated IDs cannot be changed. Instead, users will need to log in using the 'Sign-in with CLO-SET' option starting from CLO version 2024.0 and above. (*both on the CLO website and the CLO software) You can change your email address. To do so, please visit your Account page. For detailed instructions, please refer to the related article: **[Change Email from CLO-SET](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/31866962710169-Change-Email-from-CLO-SET)** * * * *Please note that changing your email address of your CLO-SET account does not affect your activated licenses or subscription status.
content_description: This webpage provides guidance on managing your CLO-SET account, specifically addressing how to change your email address while noting that auto-generated IDs cannot be modified.

title: [Style Property] Topstitch Length (SPI) (ver4.1.0 and Above)
content: **List of Contents** Length (SPI) Space **Objective** SPI stands for Stitch Per Inch, meaning the number of stitches within an inch. For example, 'SPI-4' means there are four individual stitches within an inch. For standard garments, SPI-11 is often being used. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Topstitch ▶ Topstitch Property Editor ▶ **Length (SPI)** **Operation** **Length (SPI)** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch ▶ Topstitch Property Editor ▶ **Length (SPI)** 2. Adjust the number of stitches within an inch. **Space** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch ▶ Topstitch Property Editor ▶ **Space** 2. Adjust the distance between each stitch. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide on adjusting Stitch Per Inch (SPI) and spacing for topstitching in garment design.

title: USD File Import/ Export (ver 2024.0)
content: **List of Contents** **Import** **Export** ### ### **Objective ** As one of the graphics standard file formats, USD allows you to increase productivity in collaboration with various 3D software. ### **Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import/ Import (Add)/ Export ▶ USD ### **Operation** **Import** 1. Click the tool /menu in Location. → The Open File window opens. 2. Select the desired file and click the **Open** button. → Import USD window opens. 3. Set the details and click the **OK** button. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Load Type** | Open or add new files. **Object Type** | Select the object type(Avatar, Trims, Scene and Props) of the USD file to be imported. **Scale** | Type in the Scale or select the desired unit. **Translation** | Click the "Align Bottom to Ground" option to set the location of the file as needed. **※ Note:** If you import additional USD files, you can set the location of the object in the X, Y, and Z axis. **Export** 1. Click the tool /menu in Location. → The Open File window opens. 2. Select the desired location and click the Save button. → Export USD window opens. 3. Set the details and click the **OK** button. **Option** | **Description**** ** ---|--- **Prim Path** | Set whether to export Meshes and Materials, and specify the Prim Path to be dependent upon export. Materials are stored in the textures folder within the saved USD file folder. **Object**** **** ** | Select the objects you want to export (Patterns, Avatars, Graphics and Trims). ** Object** | Choose whether to export the selected objects as a single object or multiple objects. ** Thickness** | Choose to export the object with the thickness or not. **Unified UV Coordinates** | Texture information for all garment is exported within UV coordinate values between 0 and 1. **Include Garment Simulation Data** | You can achieve more dynamic clothing for your UE 5.4 scene through the updated USD export for garments, including geometry, materials, and the necessary data for simulation setup. **Scale** | Type in the Scale or select the desired unit. ****
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for importing and exporting USD files, enhancing collaboration and productivity across various 3D software platforms.

title: [Style Property] Distance from Stitch (ver4.1.0 and Above)
content: ### **Objective** Adjust distance between Topstitches when a single Topstitch style has multiple stitch counts. The **Distance from Stitch** is adjusted in inch, but it can also be adjusted in cm or mm with its child options. ** Location** Topstitch ▶ Select Topstitch Stype with Multiple Stitch Count ▶ Property Editor ▶ Number Tab ▶ **Distance from Stitch 1,2...** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Topstitch ▶ Select Topstitch Stype with Multiple Stitch Count ▶ Property Editor ▶ Number Tab ▶ **Distance from Stitch 1,2...**** ** 2. Use the drop-down menu next to the option to choose the desired number. → Distance between each Topstitch lines are adjusted accordingly. 3. Adjust **Distance from Stitch** for all Topstitches or [configure to adjust their properties at once.](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000350228)
content_description: This web page provides instructions for adjusting the distance between multiple topstitch lines in various measurement units, ensuring precise customization of stitching properties.

title: [Object Browser] Create Additional Topstitch Style
content: **Objective** Create a new Topstitch style. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ **+Add** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ **+Add** → A new item named Topstitch_1 is now being added with the same property of Default_Topstitch. **※ Note:** * Additional items are added with names of Topstitch_1,2,3…. * If there are multiple Topstitch styles in the Topstitch tab when creating a Topstitch on a Pattern, click on the desired Topstitch style and create. * To create an additional Topstitch style with existing *.sst file, navigate to the Library ▶ Hardware and Trims ▶ **Topstitch** and drag and drop the desired Topstitch style to the Topstitch tab. title: [Style Property] Topstitch Thread Thickness
content: ### **Objective** Adjust the **Thread Thickness** in the desired measurement unit: inch, millimeter (mm), or centimeter (cm). Topstitch thickness can also be adjusted in industry standard units: Tex, Ticket (Tkt), Metric (Nm), or Denier (Den) (ver4.0.0). **Location** Object Browser ▶ Topstitch ▶ Topstitch Property Editor ▶ **Thread Thickness** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch ▶ Topstitch Property Editor ▶ **Thread Thickness** → Adjust the **Thread Thickness** with the desired unit of measurement.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for adjusting thread thickness in various measurement units within the Topstitch Property Editor.

title: [Style Property] Save Created Image as Topstitch File
content: ### **Objective** Save customized Topstitch images in a *.sst format file. ### **Location** Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ **Default Topstitch** ### **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ **Default Topstitch** → Properties of the selected Topstitch appear in the Property Editor. 2. Navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Type and select **Texture** from the drop-down menu. 3. Under the **Material** section, select the same structured Topstitch to the one customized. 4. Navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Texture and then click on the Topstitch image icon or the **Search** button. → The Open file window appears. 5. Find the path to the customized images and select the one only with the name of Topstitch (ex. "zigzag.png") and click **Open**. → The program automatically saves all five images in *.sst file according to the defined naming rule. → The image is loaded in actual size which is approximately 2cm and it may look bigger than other preset Topstitches. 6. Navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Preset and enter desired value to the **Stitch Width** menu (ex. 5mm) to adjust its size. 7. On the right top of the Property Editor, there is a **Save** button. Select to save. → The Save file window appears. 8. Enter the desired name and location and save. → The Topstitch is now being saved in *.sst file format. **※ Note:** * Topstitches are classified into two different types depending on the presence and absence of the Stitch Width property. For example, when adding a zigzag-style top stitches, select Overlock or Zigzag as its width needs to be adjustable. **Without Width Property** | Default (Single Needle) ---|--- Default Offset 0 Pick Stitch **With Width Property** | Overlock Zigzag Buttonhole Bar Tack * Make sure all of the Topstitch image files are located in the same path as it will not be saved in the SST file properly. * The image is bigger than the actual size to prevent distortion in resolution when enlarging the image. * Drag and drop the saved SST file directly onto the Topstitch Item List or open it by pressing the **Open** button in the Property Editor. Adjust the property details such as the Length, Offset, Thread Thickness or Color likewise any other Topstitch styles.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for saving customized Topstitch images in a *.sst file format, ensuring proper management and application of stich properties.

title: [Style Property] Create Topstitch Image File
content: ### **Objective** Customize Topstitch images. ### **Operation ** 1. Click on the link below to download the sample Topstitch images in Photoshop file format. [Topstitch Sample Image Download](https://s3.amazonaws.com/CLOdata/Manual_Linked_File_\(DoNotDelete\)/Topstitch_Zigzag.zip) 2. Create five images of Topstitches in each different thread thickness in Adobe Photoshop. 3. Save the images followed by the rules below. →Save the images in *PNG file format. →Name the images as below: **Required File Name** | **Thread Thickness Range of Topstitch Property in Program** ---|--- ※ When modifying the thread thickness value as the right section, images will be opened as the left section. **Zigzag_vertythin.png** | 0.2 - 0.4 mm **Zigzag_thin.png** | 0.5 - 0.6 mm **Zigzag.png** | 0.7 - 1.0 mm **Zigzag_thick.png** | 1.0 - 1.5 mm **Zigzag_verythick.png** | > 1.5 mm →Save all five images in the same location. **※ Note:** * To create top-stitch images, it is needed to have editable software (ex. Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Illustrator). * To create one top-stitch, five images of each different thread thickness are required. (Five images are included in the provided Download File.) * If not creating all five images in each different thread thickness, the thread thickness is unable to be modified in spite of modifying the value in Thread Thickness in the Property Editor. * To express transparent background, the *PNG file should contains an alpha channel. [(Creating an alpha channel)](https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop/using/saving-selections-alpha-channel-masks.html) Simply save the file after adjustments as the provided Download File already includes an alpha channel. * When saving a newly loaded Topstitch style into a file, the program automatically loads all five images and save, all of the images should be in the same path or location in order to work properly.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for customizing Topstitch images in Adobe Photoshop, ensuring all necessary images are created and saved correctly for optimal functionality.

title: [Object Browser] Puckering List Window
content: It is possible to create, copy, apply and set a style in puckering list window. Without any extra setting, Default_Puckering is applied as default. Once Default_Puckering style is modified, it lasts until rerun of the program and it is unable to be deleted.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on creating, copying, and applying styles in the puckering list window, highlighting the persistent nature of the Default_Puckering style.

title: [Style Property] Number of Topstitch Line Setting
content: ### **Objective** Set how many lines of Topstitches there are for a single style. ** Location** Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ **Number of Lines** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ **Number of Lines** 2. Enter the number of lines as desired. → The **Number of Lines** is now being adjusted and applied. **※ Note :** **Distance of Number of Lines** It is possible to adjust the distance between the lines. The unit of the length can be set in inch, millimeter(mm) or centimeter(cm). When alteration is made in inch(in), it automatically appears in millimeter(mm) or centimeter(cm) and vice versa.
content_description: This webpage aims to guide users in adjusting the number of lines of Topstitches for a specific style, including options for line spacing and measurement units.

title: Import - OBJ
content: **List of Contents** Import OBJ Import (Add) OBJ **Import OBJ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fjrW762CniQ \- OBJs can be used as Avatars or other background props compose the 3D environment. \- The 3D Garments created in CLO can be exported as an OBJ to use in other 3D software. \- When a 3D Garment is exported as an OBJ, the file will contain MTL file which saves the texture information. \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select File ▶ Import ▶ **OBJ. ** \- Locate the OBJ file and select **Open.** \- The Import OBJ window will appear. \- **Load Type** : Select either to open or add the OBJ file. \- **Object Type** : select the type of the OBJ file \- **Scale** : select the unit of the OBJ When the**Auto Scale** option is selected, CLO will detect the unit of the OBJ automatically. \- Axis Conversion: Change the axis of the OBJ. \- Translation: designate the position of the OBJ. \- Select OK to open the OBJ based on the settings. ** Import (Add) OBJ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IyutFBV0R2Q \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select File ▶ Import (Add) ▶ **OBJ. ** \- Locate the OBJ file and select **Open.** \- The selected OBJ file will be added to the workspace. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on importing and adding OBJ files in CLO software, complete with step-by-step instructions and helpful video tutorials.

Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Internal Point) ▶**Internal Point** → The Internal Line is divided at the selected point. → The divided point is now indicated as a point with no fill. **Divide Internal Line** 1. Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001095927/2.png)**Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. 2. content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for using the Divide Internal Point and Divide Internal Line functions to effectively cut and separate internal elements within a design.

content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide instructions for displaying all piping in a 3D window using the "Show All Piping" feature from the right-click menu.

title: Reset 2D Arrangement (Selected)
content: **Reset 2D Arrangement (Selected)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T4PCSgMtL98 \- Re-arrange 3D Patterns according to the Pattern arrangement in the 2D window. \- Right-click on the Pattern to be re-arranged and select **Reset 2D Arrangement (Selected)** from the pop-up menu. \- Selected Patterns will be re-arranged in the 3D window reflecting the Pattern arrangement in the 2D window.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for resetting the arrangement of selected 3D patterns to match their layout in a 2D window using a simple right-click action.

title: Flip Normal
content: **Flip Normal** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXAxw-7CpbM \- Easily flip the Pattern inside-out. \- Choose the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021552387/mceclip0.png) **Select/Move** tool from 3D toolbar and navigate to the 3D window. \- Right-click on the 3D Garment and select **Flip Normal.** \- The selected Pattern will flip inside-out, face side will flip to the backside and vice-versa. \- When Fold Angles are assigned to the flipped Pattern, Fold Angles will be reversed.
content_description: Learn how to easily flip your garment patterns inside-out in CLO3D by using the Flip Normal feature in this step-by-step guide.

title: Pin – Delete All Pins
content: **Pin - Delete All Pins** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WwHlVqLVnBY \- Delete all pins on the 3D Garment. \- Choose the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021552387/mceclip0.png) **Select****/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar and navigate to the 3D window. \- Right-click on the 3D Garment and Select pin ▶ **Delete All Pins.** \- All pins created on the 3D Garment will be deleted.
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide on how to delete all pins from a 3D garment using the Select/Move tool in Clo3D.

title: Lock All Internal Lines
content: **Lock All Internal Lines** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DcZtWcbZMvU \- Lock all Internal Lines to inhibit selecting and editing in the 2D window. \- Right-click on the 2D window and select **Lock All Internal Lines** from the pop-up menu. All Internal Lines will turn grey and be deactivated. \- Only activated Patterns can be selected and edited.
content_description: This webpage provides a quick guide on how to lock all internal lines in the 2D window to prevent accidental selection and editing, ensuring that only activated patterns can be modified.

title: Superimpose (Under)
content: **Superimpose (Under)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oBF_n-nI2b0 \- When a Pattern is sewn to another Pattern, place one below the other’s surface based on the Sewing Lines. \- Choose the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021552387/mceclip0.png) **Select****/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar and navigate to the 3D window. \- Right-click on the 3D Garment and select **Superimpose (Under).** \- The selected Pattern will be arranged under the sewn pair along its surface. \- The Superimpose (Under) function can be used only when two Patterns are sewn to each other.
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide on using the Superimpose (Under) feature in garment design software to effectively layer sewn patterns based on their sewing lines.

title: Superimpose (Side)
content: **Superimpose (Side)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RxcdD-agS9s \- When a Pattern is sewn to another Pattern, place one next to the other’s side based on the Sewing Lines. \- Choose the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021552387/mceclip0.png) **Select/****Move** tool from the 3D toolbar and navigate to the 3D window. \- Right-click on the 3D Garment and select Superimpose (Side). \- The selected Pattern will be arranged next to the sewn pair along its side. \- The Superimpose (Side) function can be used only when two Patterns are sewn to each other.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to use the Superimpose (Side) function in Clo3D to arrange patterns next to each other based on sewing lines.
